title: Human Evolution
hook: We didn't descend from chimpanzees — we share an ancestor with them. From that branching point, our lineage walked upright, grew big brains, and spread across the planet.
key_points: Humans and chimpanzees share a common ancestor that lived roughly 6–8 million years ago.
Walking upright (bipedalism) came early, well before our brains enlarged.
Stone tools, controlled fire, and growing brain size mark the genus Homo.
Homo sapiens arose in Africa around 300,000 years ago, then spread worldwide.
content_html: A persistent myth says humans evolved from chimpanzees. We didn't — chimps are our cousins, not our grandparents. Both lineages trace back to a common ancestor that lived around six to eight million years ago, and each has been evolving on its own path ever since. Our branch is studied through fossils of species like Australopithecus, Homo erectus, and the Neanderthals, which document how upright walking, tool use, and large brains accumulated over time rather than all at once.
extra_html: The order of those changes is one of the field's big surprises. Bipedalism — walking on two legs — came early; ancestors like "Lucy" (Australopithecus afarensis) strode upright more than three million years ago while still carrying ape-sized brains. Stone tools, controlled use of fire, and dramatic brain expansion arrived later, marking the genus Homo. Our own species, Homo sapiens, emerged in Africa roughly 300,000 years ago and eventually spread across every continent, at times overlapping and even interbreeding with relatives like Neanderthals. The Smithsonian's Human Origins program traces this branching family tree and is careful to stress that human evolution is a bush, not a ladder — many human species once existed, and we are the lone survivors.

source.name: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History — Human Origins

related.title: The Tree of Life
related.hook: Humans, mushrooms, and oak trees share an ancestor if you go back far enough — all life on Earth branches from a single common root.

related.title: The Evidence for Evolution
related.hook: Fossils, DNA, shared body plans, and change we can watch happen — evolution isn't a hunch, it's a conclusion forced by many independent lines of evidence.

flashcards.prompt: What is the relationship between humans and chimpanzees?

choices.text: We share a common ancestor that lived millions of years ago
Humans evolved directly from modern chimpanzees
There is no evolutionary connection between them

flashcards.explanation_html: Humans did not descend from living chimps. The two lineages split from a shared ancestor roughly 6–8 million years ago and have evolved separately since.

flashcards.prompt: In human evolution, which came first?

choices.text: Both appeared at exactly the same moment

flashcards.explanation_html: Early human ancestors like Australopithecus walked upright while still having ape-sized brains. Large brains evolved much later in the genus Homo.

flashcards.prompt: Where and roughly when did Homo sapiens first appear?
flashcards.back_html: In Africa, about 300,000 years ago. Our species later spread out of Africa to populate the rest of the world.
